clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 1 and 2 for 0x4cd3be8768aea2a0297c22c17a7a3cae65adc0cc (bits 0xcc, swap return delta flags), code on Base only, pools with liquidity on Arbitrum One, Polygon, OP Mainnet and BNB Smart Chain: who can place code at it and who holds a role after a replay.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Rerun independently (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-hook-replay.verify/spot_onchain.json and spot_sim_0x4cd3be87.json). eth_getCode of the hook is 0x on Arbitrum One (nitro v3.13.0-rc.9, block 527,682,479), BNB Smart Chain (Geth v1.8.2, block 135,818,266) and OP Mainnet (op-reth, block 160,042,257); 0x4e59b448 has 69 bytes on all three; eth_call of raw/init_0x69dee05880.hex to 0x4e59b448 from a different sender (0x...beef) returns 0x4cd3be87...c0cc on all three, so any account can fill the address. The runtime read from Base today (21,565 bytes, SHA-256 457f6061...64ba) equals the constructor output in raw/ctor_runtime_0x4cd3be87.hex, contains the Base PoolManager 0x498581ff five times and the Arbitrum PoolManager 0x360e68fa zero times. With that runtime and owner slots 0 and 9 = 0x2cd52439 placed by state override, beforeSwap called from the local PoolManager reverts with 0xae18210a on Arbitrum One and BNB Smart Chain, and keccak256('NotPoolManager()')[:4] = ae18210a. Code side: 0xcc sets bits 7, 6, 3 and 2 only (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:38-45), so add and remove liquidity and donate make no hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:195-243), and a revert in beforeSwap bubbles out of callHook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-138), so swaps revert as they do today against the empty address. Swap return deltas never reach the hook's code path. No stranger gains a role or a claim on amounts.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Tasks 1 and 2 for 0x3a3a9a072ab438335a52e0cf064f7ec91d824080 (bit 0x80, Unichain pool 0x358bebb5 with liquidity): nobody but the original key can fill it on Unichain.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On Unichain (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, block 64,934,933) the hook 0x3a3a9a07, the implementation 0xcc42bf29 and the factory 0x0bde0085 all have code 0x, and 0xff64a8a1 has nonce 0 and no code (no EIP-7702 designation), so 0xcc42bf29, a CREATE address of 0xff64a8a1 at nonce 147 per raw/findtx_0xcc42bf29_24283267.json, can only appear after that key sends 147 transactions there. The earlier replay eth_call on Unichain reverts (raw/replaycall_0x3a3a9a07_130.json), consistent with the proxy constructor refusing an empty implementation. Bit 0x80 alone gives a hook no delta (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:38, 248-315 need bit 3 for a return delta), so even the key holder could only block swaps, not take amounts.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Tasks 1 and 2 for 0x74803bd586fa5ce3a9ab38b49a7ca633af8700cc (bits 0xcc, swap return delta flags, Unichain pool 0xba03dec3) and 0x4440854b (bits 0xc4): only one private key per address can fill them on Unichain.
clearedSpotChecks.note: On Unichain at block 64,934,933 the hook 0x74803bd5 and its factory 0x0bde0085 have code 0x and 0x75d59285 has nonce 0 and no code, matching raw/hook_7480.json. The factory on Ethereum came from a type 2 CREATE with chainId 1 at nonce 0 of 0x75d59285, so a stranger cannot place the factory and therefore cannot place the hook. If that key holder did rebuild it, the actor would be the hook author (pool-creator), not a stranger. The 0x4440854b part (factory 0x8cad6a96 empty on Unichain per raw/factory_presence.json) was not requeried in this check; its pool holds no liquidity.
